heard: A massive asteroid blindsided Earth while astronomers watched a different rock. On February 15, 2013, scientists focused on asteroid Duende making a close flyby. But hidden in the sun's glare, a 10,000-ton asteroid approached entirely undetected. Measuring 18 meters wide, it slammed into the atmosphere at 19 kilometers per second. 30 kilometers up, the rock exploded with 30 times the energy of the Hiroshima bomb. The blast was briefly brighter than the sun, shattering windows and injuring 1,500 people. Orbits proved these two asteroids were unrelated, but the Stryker had its own violent history. That history ended when a massive asteroid blindsided Earth while astronomers watched a different rock.
